question: What is the meaning of picture in relation to physical properties, technical properties?
description: The picture illustrates the various physical properties relevant to sustainable construction, such as dimensions, weight, density, building physics, energy and thermal performance, heat transfer coefficient, thermal mass, absorption, thermal conductivity, heat protection, transparency, hygroscopicity, sound insulation and transfer, fire protection, ventilation and air tightness, day lighting and illumination properties, resistance and rigidity, expected lifetime, tensile strength, testing, actively beneficial functions, ease of recycling and reuse, and others. These properties are essential for evaluating the sustainability and performance of construction materials and products. Technical properties, while not explicitly mentioned in the picture, would likely include aspects such as manufacturing processes, durability, and compatibility with other materials, which are also important for sustainable construction.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.
